approved_text: Let fs be a finite set of nonconstant irreducible integer polynomials with positive leading coefficients. Suppose that for every prime p there is a natural number n with p dividing no f(n), f in fs. Then infinitely many natural numbers n make |f(n)| prime for every f in fs.
draft: Let fs be a finite set of integer polynomials. Suppose each satisfies the Bunyakovsky condition (irreducible, positive leading coefficient, values with no common prime divisor). Suppose also that no prime p divides the product of all f(n) for every n. Then infinitely many natural numbers n make |f(n)| prime for every f in fs.
source_docstrings:
**Schinzel conjecture (H hypothesis)**
If a finite set of polynomials $f_i$ satisfies both Schinzel and Bunyakovsky conditions,
there exist infinitely many natural numbers $n$ such that $f_i(n)$ are primes for all $i$.
source_lean:
theorem schinzel_conjecture (fs : Finset ℤ[X]) (hfs : ∀ f ∈ fs, BunyakovskyCondition f)
    (hfs' : SchinzelCondition fs) : Infinite {n : ℕ | ∀ f ∈ fs, (f.eval (n : ℤ)).natAbs.Prime}
